# Agent OS — Architecture  Most agent stacks hardcode a model name into every call site. Agent OS does the opposite. A capability is a seat — a logical slot like fast, reader, coder, or judge — and each seat self-reports the task KINDS it can serve. The router builds a by_kind index at runtime and resolves kind → capable seat on every task, so swapping providers, adding a local model, or wiring an MCP tool never touches your call sites. Around that router sits a kernel that runs a goal in cycles

# MYRIAD — Architecture  MYRIAD is self-play for LLM agents. Given a task, it proposes K attempts along fixed, distinct reasoning angles, fans them out through any model you inject, scores each with a DETERMINISTIC verifier you control (never a model grading its own work), and computes each attempt's group-relative advantage with critic-free GRPO. The best variant is the answer; the spread becomes a lesson you can distill into a policy. No gradient step, no training loop, no judge model — just s

# Output Speed — Architecture  Output Speed encodes a simple truth: LLM wall-clock scales roughly linearly with the tokens you ask a model to emit. So the biggest free speedup is emitting fewer of them. budgetFor(kind) right-sizes max_tokens per task kind (a classification never gets a 4000-token budget; a code file never gets starved below its floor). fastLane(kind) names the fastest seat that is still capable of the kind — mechanical work on a fast low-effort seat, judging on a strong one. tri

# Memory — Architecture  Give your agent a memory that survives every session without a vector database, an embedder, or a server. Memory keeps two things on disk: self-editing core blocks that are always in context (persona, the human, working notes), and an append-only archival log you can recall from. # Bugbot — Architecture  Bugbot reviews unified diffs, not whole repos. A FINDER model traces data flow and error paths across the changed hunks and proposes candidate findings under strict noise rules (no style, no nits — only logic bugs, leaks, races, broken error handling, security, and contract breaks). Every candidate then faces a REFUTER: a second adversarial pass whose default verdict is KILL and which must fail to disprove a finding before it surfaces. Findings arrive as structured JSON

# Fusion — Architecture  Fusion is a front door for LLM work that picks the cheapest lane that still gets the right answer. Trivial tasks go to a single model. Homogeneous batches run speculative batch-fusion — draft cheap, verify the whole block in one judge pass, re-work only what fails. Hard or high-stakes tasks get the full panel: an author drafts, a second model cross-watches and refines, and a judge does a final correctness-and-elevate pass. The method call carries a `StreamRef`, a handle a few dozen bytes long; the bytes travel beside it.
